prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for its experimental discovery in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I opened with circuit QED (B042) first, and I still think it is the best-documented case on this list for technological consequence. After reading all eight ballots I move my preferred configuration to B044. Six of eight members ranked it, four placed it in their top three and two placed it first, and the support comes from members whose own fields are far apart (Danielsson, Olsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Kroll and I). The case is a rare clean pairing of theory and experiment. Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal, and Molenkamp's group observed the helical edge channels in HgTe/CdTe wells. Nearly two decades of independent confirmation by transport and ARPES, across HgTe, InAs/GaSb and three-dimensional materials, have made the interpretation stable. The result also feeds directly into my own area, since protected edge states and topological superconductivity underlie the Majorana proposals that many superconducting-circuit groups study. A three-name prize on one achievement is coherent and matches the credited names.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted that HgTe/CdTe would show the effect, and König et al. is the experiment Molenkamp's group reported. The three-dimensional work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore and Balents; Roy; Hsieh and Hasan) is also not in the credited set, so any three-name prize leaves out people with real claims. A second concern is overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phases of matter. A committee could judge that the theme is partly recognised already and the recognition less urgent. Finally, the 2025 prize has just gone to superconducting circuits, which may make the committee less ready to consider B042 in the next few years. That does not lower the scientific standing of the topological work.

responses.point: Danielsson puts B044 first as a clean prediction followed by a decisive experiment that opened topological band theory, and flags the credit overlap with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D topological insulator work.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific case and it has moved my own ranking from fifth to first. I would go further on the attribution problem than Danielsson does. If the committee wants the experimental half to carry a name, Molenkamp is the only experimentalist in the credited set, and the prize should say 'discovery in HgTe quantum wells' so that the citation does not claim the 3D work. I do not think the BHZ gap disqualifies the candidate. It is a genuine limit of a three-person prize, and the citation wording has to be careful instead of expanding the list.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the optical lattice clock (B024) first, as a concrete and mature invention that took clock uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and is already reproduced in many laboratories, and ranks B044 third as mature but partly covered by the 2016 prize.
responses.response: I take the 2016 overlap seriously and I share it as a reservation, but the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and quantum Hall topology, not the time-reversal-invariant Z2 classification or the quantum spin Hall edge states. I therefore treat the two as distinct achievements. I also think B024 is the strongest alternative and I name it as such. My reservation is that it is chiefly a measurement invention with a fundamental-physics payoff, such as the redefinition of the second and constants tests, that is still developing, and the 2005 and 2012 prizes already covered the comb and ion-clock routes. That is a question of timing and not a flaw in the science.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B024 first as the clearest case of better measurement opening new physics and notes that the quantum-computing landscape after the 2025 circuit prize is delicate.
responses.response: Kroll is right about the delicacy, and I find it a reason to put my own first-place candidate B042 behind both B044 and B024 in this round. The 2025 prize covered macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in a circuit. Circuit QED is a different achievement, but the committee would be criticised for returning to superconducting circuits so soon. I disagree with Kroll only in degree on B024. I find its metrology case persuasive, but B044 has broader support and a stronger discovery character.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube (B019) first as a real discovery about cosmic accelerators that needed a remarkable instrument, with a sole credited name, Francis Halzen.
responses.response: I respect the discovery, and the diffuse flux and the source evidence are well established. I do not support a sole-laureate prize for a large-collaboration observatory when the credited set contains one person. That would hide the people who built and operated the detector. Only two of eight members ranked B019, and I would want a credit set that spans the instrument builders before moving it into my top choices.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a three-name prize that leaves out Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological insulator contributors, and how far the citation should be restricted to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect.
How much the 2016 prize for topological phases of matter reduces the priority of B044.
Whether the 2025 prize makes B042 premature for the committee, and whether a four-name credited set (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin) could be cut to three without an unfair omission.
statement.conflict_note: B042 (circuit QED) is my own field and I opened with it first, so I should recuse myself from any decision on it. I work in superconducting circuits and microwave quantum optics at Chalmers and direct WACQT, and my profile lists Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and frequent co-author Anton Frisk Kockum. Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. None of this bears on B044, which I prefer, and no specific conflict is apparent with B044 or B024 from the provided profile.
